comments.comment: On today's episode of statements that contradict themselves:
Not regretting the decision doesn’t mean you don’t regret the circumstances that made it the decision you chose.
i wish i lived in a society that supported pregnant women and mothers instead of making them face this awful choice.

@prolifeisalie I adopted a five year old who was recommended for a late term abortion for her many severe disabilities. She’s 13 now and requires full-time care, probably for life. I’m happy to do it because her life matters.

I don’t think your characterization of a pro-lifer applies to me, nor does it apply to my daughter’s biological mother, who was pressured at every point to abort “for your health and for that of the healthy twin.” Trust me, we both think about abortion *every day,* that it could have ended our girl’s beating heart in a violent, cruel, barbaric manner.
How is this any different than a mother who kills her toddler? “I still grieve the loss of my toddler, but I don’t regret my decision.”
One can have grief without regret but it’s hard to have grief without lingering trauma.
